header.running_head: Reproaching Those who Question the Mutashaabih Verses of the Qur'aan

blocks.text: Reproaching Those who Question the Mutashaabih[^1] Verses of the Qur'aan
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Reproaches Sabeegh for Questioning the Mutashaabih Verses of the Qur'aan

A freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that an Iraqi called Sabeegh in the Muslim army was questioning certain (Mutashaabih) verses of the Qur'aan and continued doing so until he reached Egypt. From there, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) sent him to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA). A messenger brought the letter to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and after he had read it, he asked, "Where is the man?" "He is still on the carriage," replied the messenger. Hadhrat Umar (RA) instructed, "Go see if he is still there because I will punish you very severely if he has escaped." When Sabeegh came, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to him, "What are your questions?" When he stated his case, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) for a branch of a date palm. He then beat the man until his back was scarred. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then left him until his wounds healed. Thereafter, he repeated the treatment and again left him to recover. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) called him back for more of the same, Sabeegh pleaded with him saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! If you wish to kill me, do so in a nice manner and if you intend to cure me, then I swear by Allaah that I have already been cured." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then permitted him to return to his land but sent a letter with him to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) stating that none of the Muslims should associate with him. When this became unbearable for him, Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) wrote back to Hadhrat Umar (RA) stating that Sabeegh had truly reformed. It was only then that Hadhrat Umar (RA) permitted the people to associate with him. [^2]

Another narration from Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar states that a man from the Banu Tameem called Sabeegh bin Isl once arrived in Madinah. He had many books and always questioned the Mutashaabih verses of the Qur'aan. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard about this, he sent for Sabeegh while keeping some branches of the date palm ready for him. When he arrived, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him who he was. "I am the servant of Allaah, Sabeegh," came the reply. "And I am the servant of Allaah, Umar!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) retorted. Mutashaabih (plural - Mutashaabihaat): These are those verses of the Qur'aan that are not as clear as the "Muhkamaat" in their interpretation. Their meanings are best known to Allaah. Allaah says about these verses, "None knows their interpretation except Allaah" [Surah 3, verse 7]. It is necessary to interpret these verses only in a manner that does not contradict what the Muhkam verses mention. When a suitable interpretation cannot be found, one should not delve too deeply into their meanings because the injunctions of Islaam are clearly mentioned in the Muhkamaat verses and failure to perfectly interpret the Mutashaabih verses will not affect a person's life.
Daarmi, Ibn Abdil Hakam and Ibn Asaakir.
